dedupe_keys.name: tracing opioids across the us reconstructed pharmaceutical distribution paths from dea arcos 2006 2014

description: This data set traces how individual packages of controlled drugs, mainly opioids, moved through the United States pharmaceutical supply chain from manufacturers through distributors to about 300,000 pharmacies, hospitals and practitioners. The authors reconstructed 375 million complete distribution paths for 18,672 drug products from ARCOS, the Drug Enforcement Administration's database of about half a billion shipment records between registrants, which records only single hops. The producers are Ambra Amico, Luca Verginer and Frank Schweitzer, who describe it in Scientific Data (2024). Coverage is national, 2006 to 2014, covering more than 1,800 distributors and manufacturers. Each product has a JSONL file listing, for every path, the sequence of distributors by DEA number, the shipping dates and the quantity delivered, with supporting tables of entities and product codes; the collection on figshare includes the processing code and is released under CC0, as a 3.6 GB archive that expands to about 50 GiB. Caveats: paths in early 2006 are less reliable because starting stocks are unknown, the data stop in 2014, and only drugs reported to ARCOS are included. Simulation uses: network models of pharmaceutical distribution, tests of how the failure of a distributor or a disaster region cascades to hospital and pharmacy supply, and calibration of drug shortage models. Related records: openFDA food enforcement (data-openfda-food-enforcement) shows a comparable recall stream for food, and the CMS hospital provider data (data-cms-provider-data-hospitals) lists hospitals.
